ins: In the 1860s and 1870s Scottish, Irish, and English immigrants, attracted by the lumber boom, settled in Taymouth Township. In 1873 they established St. Paul’s Episcopal Mission and the following year built this Gothic Revival-inspired church. The community’s Episcopalian population soon declined and by 1893 services were being held monthly. The last service was held in 1909. Since 1920 Taymouth Township has owned the building, which retains its original form and trim.

ph.alt: Side view of a small single story church with a bell tower on the left end.

f: Burt Rd. at Flint River, Taymouth Township
wx: The Morseville Bridge is a bridge which formerly carried Burt Road over the Flint River in Taymouth Township, Michigan. It was listed on the National Register of Historic Places in 1990.
